transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

Hi doctor. I've been having a really hard time staying in my seat lately, whether I'm at work in meetings or out at dinner. I just feel this constant urge to get up and move around, and it's starting to cause some real issues for me.

Have you ever had a period lasting several days when you felt unusually energetic or euphoric, needed much less sleep, and were more impulsive or talkative than usual? Or has this restlessness been more constant over time?

No, I've never had those short phases of feeling euphoric or needing less sleep. This restlessness and my tendency to talk too much have been constant for about a year and two months now, and honestly, these kinds of struggles go all the way back to when I was a kid before age 12.
Along with the restlessness and talking a lot, do you also often have trouble paying attention, staying organized, or finishing tasks? For example, do you get easily distracted or lose things often?

I definitely struggle with paying attention, mostly because I tend to make a lot of careless mistakes and miss important details. I'm not really sure about losing things or having trouble with organization, as those aren't really issues for me. It's really just the careless errors and lack of attention to detail that I notice happening a lot.

Besides careless mistakes, do you also often have trouble staying focused on tasks or conversations, avoiding tasks that need sustained mental effort, or not seeming to listen when spoken to directly?

No, I don't really experience those specific difficulties with staying focused, avoiding tasks, or not listening. Like I mentioned, my main issue in that area is just making careless mistakes and missing details.
Besides difficulty staying seated and talking a lot, do you often feel driven like a motor, blurt out answers, interrupt others, or have trouble waiting your turn?

No, I don't really experience those things—I don't feel driven by a motor, blurt out answers, or have trouble waiting my turn. For me, the real challenges are definitely just my struggle to stay in my seat and my tendency to talk excessively.
Do these symptoms cause problems in more than one setting, like both work and home or social situations, and have they been present most of the time for at least 6 months?

Yes, these symptoms have been going on constantly for about a year and two months now, so well over six months. They definitely cause a lot of trouble in multiple places, both at work and at home, especially with my tendency to make careless mistakes, talk excessively, and struggle to stay in my seat.
Before age 12, did you also have several other attention problems besides careless mistakes, like being easily distracted, losing things, forgetting tasks, or not finishing schoolwork?

I don't really recall having those specific problems like losing things, forgetting tasks, or being easily distracted before age 12. Back then, it was really just the careless mistakes and struggling to sit still.
Before age 12, besides struggling to sit still, did you also often talk excessively, fidget, run about when it wasn’t appropriate, or have trouble doing quiet activities calmly?
Yes, even before I turned 12, I definitely struggled with talking excessively. I also constantly left my seat when I was expected to stay put, which was a big issue for me back then too.
Before age 12, did you also often fidget, run or climb when it wasn’t appropriate, or have trouble playing or doing quiet activities calmly?
I don't recall having those specific issues before age 12. I don't remember fidgeting, running or climbing around inappropriately, or struggling to do quiet activities calmly back then.
Before age 12, did you often interrupt others, blurt out answers, or have trouble waiting your turn?
No, I don't recall having those specific issues when I was younger. I don't remember interrupting people, blurting out answers, or having trouble waiting my turn.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a persistent pattern since childhood of hyperactive/impulsive symptoms centered on difficulty remaining seated and excessive talking, with symptoms present for over 6 months, onset before age 12, and impairment across work and home settings. Inattentive symptoms are limited and do not meet threshold, and there is no evidence of episodic mania to suggest a bipolar disorder.
